title: Counting attackers and defenders

D0.outcome: Says that a piece is defended by the pieces that could recapture on its square, and that attackers and defenders can be counted.

D1.outcome: Counts the attackers and the defenders of a given square (direct attacks only, kings included).

D2.outcome: Decides whether to take a defended piece by comparing what is won and what may be lost, capturing with the cheapest attacker first.

D3.outcome: States when the simple count cannot be trusted: a pinned defender, an overloaded defender, or a piece standing behind another on the same line.

misconceptions: The side with more attackers than defenders always wins the exchange.
The order of captures does not matter.
A defender that is pinned or overloaded still counts as a defender.
conditions: Count the attackers and the defenders of the square, then play the captures out with the cheapest piece first and stop when the next capture loses.
The simple count is only valid when no attacker or defender is pinned or overloaded and no piece stands behind another on the same line.
contrasts: More attackers than defenders does not win material when the first capture is made by a piece worth more than what it takes.
A pinned or overloaded defender still counts in the simple count, which is why those cases are taught later.
Pieces that neither attack nor defend the square do not change the count.
